summary.short: Amends Georgia Code Section 31-12-12 on the sale, dispensing and prescribing of contact lenses and spectacles. Allows licensed prescribers to use AI or other 'assessment mechanisms' for eye assessments under listed conditions, and sets penalties for violations. Applies within Georgia; the document states no effective date.
summary.long: Amends Code Section 31-12-12 of the Official Code of Georgia Annotated on the sale, dispensing and prescribing of contact lenses and spectacles. Defines 'assessment mechanism', including artificial intelligence devices, and 'eye assessment'. Only persons licensed under specified Title 43 chapters may sell or dispense these products, and only a prescriber (a licensed optometrist or ophthalmologist) may write a prescription. A prescription requires an eye examination or, under stated conditions, an eye assessment. A prescriber using an assessment mechanism must meet listed conditions: the standard of care, no sole reliance on assessment data, a medical record kept for seven years, verification that the patient is 21 to 50 years old, specified exclusions, a recent eye examination, liability insurance, and disclosure to the patient with acceptance as a term of use. An assessment cannot generate an initial contact lens prescription. Assessment mechanisms must comply with telehealth, HIPAA and ADA requirements. Violations are misdemeanors or felonies depending on repetition, and a civil penalty of up to $11,000 per violation is payable to the Office of the Attorney General. Licensing boards may promulgate rules and may bring civil proceedings. Section 2 repeals conflicting laws. The text states no effective date.

notes: No effective date or governor's signature appears in the document; it is headed AS PASSED HOUSE AND SENATE. The long title refers to physicians, but the text's prescriber means only an optometrist or ophthalmologist licensed in Georgia. Stray numerals appear inside the text (e.g., subsection (d) 76 in (b)(1)(C), and 93, 121, 144, 156), apparently page or line markers. Subsections (a)(11) and (a)(12) cite Code 65 Section and Code 67 Section, which appear to be citation errors. Criminal penalties in (b)(2) and the civil penalty in (o) both apply to dispensing violations. No registry IDs were available for Georgia Code or federal acts, so target_instrument_id is empty.

'Assessment mechanism' means automated or virtual equipment, application, or technology designed to be used on a telephone, a computer, or an internet accessible device
'Contact lens' means any lens placed directly on the surface of the eye
'Dispense' means the act of furnishing spectacles or contact lenses to an individual.
'Eye assessment' means an assessment of the ocular health and visual status of a patient
'Eye examination' means a real-time examination, which includes the use of telemedicine
'Kiosk' means automatic equipment or application designed to be used on a telephone, a computer, or an internet based device
'Over-the-counter spectacles' means eyeglasses or lenses in a frame for the correction of vision that may be sold by any person, firm, or corporation at retail without a prescription
'Prescriber' means an optometrist or ophthalmologist licensed in this state.
'Prescription' means a handwritten or electronic order issued by a prescriber.
'Spectacles' means an optical instrument or device worn or used by an individual that has one or more lenses designed to correct or enhance vision
'Telehealth' has the same meaning as in paragraph (6)
'Telemedicine' has the same meaning as in paragraph (7)

obligations.summary: Where an eye examination is conducted via telemedicine, the patient and prescriber must be in synchronous verbal and visual contact during the parts of the examination necessary to make it at least equivalent to an in-person examination.

evidence.quote: the patient and prescriber shall be required to be in synchronous verbal and visual contact

obligations.summary: No person in the state may sell, dispense, or act as a conduit for the sale or dispensing of contact lenses or spectacles to the ultimate user, except persons licensed and regulated under Chapter 29, 30, or 34 of Title 43.

evidence.quote: No person in this state shall sell, dispense, or serve as a conduit for the sale or dispensing of contact lenses or spectacles to the ultimate user

obligations.summary: No person may write a prescription for contact lenses or spectacles unless they are a prescriber; no prescription may be written unless an eye examination is conducted or, under subsection (d), an eye assessment is performed; and no initial contact lens prescription may be written until the prescriber has completed the measurements, tests and fitting required for professional judgment.

evidence.quote: No person in this state shall write a prescription for contact lenses or spectacles

obligations.summary: The prescriber must give the patient a copy of the contact lens prescription upon completion of the fit.

evidence.quote: The patient shall be entitled to receive a copy of the contact lens prescription upon completion of fit.

obligations.summary: An assessment mechanism used to conduct an eye assessment or generate a prescription must be conducted under the Georgia Telehealth Act, collect the patient's medical history, prior prescription information and time since the last in-person eye examination, provide ADA-required accommodations, and perform any applicable AMA CPT-coded procedure.

obligations.summary: A prescriber using an assessment mechanism must be licensed in good standing in Georgia, act within scope of practice, and conform to the standard of eye healthcare expected in traditional in-person settings; must provide a handwritten or electronic signature with state licensure number; and must maintain liability insurance through its owner or lessee for claims based on assessment mechanism data.

evidence.quote: Conform to the standard of eye healthcare expected of traditional in-person clinical settings

obligations.summary: A prescriber may not use data or information from an eye assessment as the sole basis for issuing a prescription.

evidence.quote: Not use the data or information obtained from an eye assessment as the sole basis for issuing a prescription

obligations.summary: A prescriber must create and maintain for at least seven years a medical record for each patient, in compliance with state and federal laws.

evidence.quote: Create and maintain for at least seven years a medical record for each patient

obligations.summary: A prescriber must read and interpret the diagnostic information and data, including photographs and scans, gathered by the assessment mechanism.

evidence.quote: Read and interpret the diagnostic information and data, including any photographs

obligations.summary: A prescriber must verify the patient's identity; confirm the patient is not experiencing listed eye conditions and is not taking medications with potentially serious ocular side effects; for spectacles, verify an eye examination by a prescriber within the previous 24 months; for contact lenses, verify eye examinations at the initial and first renewal prescriptions and within 24 months after the first renewal.

evidence.quote: Verify the identity of the patient requesting treatment via the assessment mechanism

evidence.quote: Verify that the patient is between 21 and 50 years of age

obligations.summary: A prescriber must disclose to patients, and require advance acceptance as a term of use, that the eye assessment is not a replacement for an eye examination, cannot be used for an initial prescription or first renewal, and may only be used if the patient had an eye examination within the previous 24 months.

events.note: The fetched text (HB 203 as passed by House and Senate) states no dates for enactment, signature, publication, effective date or any phase-in. Section 2 repeals conflicting laws without a date. Time periods in the text (e.g., 24 months, seven years) are conditions or retention duties, not dated events of this instrument.
